questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: The recent reduction in interest rates in the US and the injection of liquidity have resulted in investors seeking new avenues such as commodity markets, in view of the turbulence in financial markets and the low returns in treasuries.

Q: The relatively easy liquidity and low interest rates, by themselves, make the holding of inventories attractive and thus induce volatility in commodity markets.

R: The financialisation of commodity trade and current extraordinary conditions in global financial markets could have influenced the spurt in prices.

S: The weakening of the US dollar is also advanced as a reason for the recent volatility in commodity markets, including food items.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **RPQS. **

The first sentence is R as it brings to the light ‘the spurt in prices’, which forms the basis of the passage.

It is followed by P, which shows the ‘reduction in interest rates’ and ‘liquidity’, followed by Q, which further expands on this topic.

It is then followed by S, which shows another reason for the ‘volatility’.

Hence, the correct combination is RPQS, as seen in **Option 4.**

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of ****labelled**** sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: While the Soviet Government bought grain and other foreign consumer goods to be sold in domestic markets at heavily subsidized rates, Russia rejected socialism.

Q: The oil industry was the prime target of a sweeping privatization drive launched after the break-up of the Soviet Union.

R: The Russian government has failed to do for its people even a fraction of what the Soviet Union, with twice the population, did with the revenue generated from oil.

S: However, not all Russian have been rolling in oil wealth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **QSRP**

The first sentence is Q since it introduces the oil industry.

It is followed by S, which brings in the Russians and oil wealth.

It is then followed by R which talks about the failure of the Russian government and references the Soviet Union, which is continued in P.

Hence, the correct combination is QSRP, as seen in **Option 1.**

questions.question:

To accept the gauntlet

options.text: To accept what is written in fate

questions.solution:

An example sentence is:

**‘He is always eager to accept the gauntlet when it comes to civil rights issues’.**

**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'. **

I was taken with surprise (1)/ when I saw (2)/ the beautiful Taj Mahal. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in **part 1** of the sentence.

The phrase **‘taken with surprise’** does not have any meaning.

The phrase **‘taken by surprise’** means **‘to shock or startle someone with an appearance’.**

Hence, the correct sentence is:

**‘I was taken by surprise when I saw the beautiful Taj Mahal’. **

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. **

I left my job because I did not (agree to) the company's appraisal policies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘agree with’**

The preposition that follows the word **agree** depends on the object. One **agrees to** **demands, agrees on issues** and **agrees with something.**

In this sentence, the company’s appraisal policies are the object. This object takes the **with **a preposition.

Hence, the correct sentence is:

**‘I left my job because I did not agree with the company’s appraisal policies’.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

I hope that I shall win this dance competition.

options.text: It is hoped that the dance competition will be won by me.
Winning the dance competition is hoped by me.
Dance competition winning is my hope.
The dance competition is hoped to be won.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘It is hoped that the dance competition will be won by me.’** 

Sentence 2 makes winning the primary subject over hope, which is incorrect as the Active voice is different.

Sentence 3 is grammatically and structurally incorrect and does not convey the same meaning.

Sentence 4 removes the ‘me’ part and completely changes the meaning of the sentence, making it incorrect.

Only **Sentence 1** retains the meaning of the sentence and accurately converts the Active voice into Passive voice.
